A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LROD/LR-YOLO research. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison. V2 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: V1 reports original detection experiments, ablations, robustness analyses, and restoration measurements, including VOC/COCO, RTTS, and ExDark results in Tables 1–9 and 12–14.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results, including the main benchmark experiments, supplementary restoration evaluation, and corrected appendix detection tables.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same shared-backbone restoration module, restoration loss, parameter-gradient regularization, and LR-YOLO architecture. No algorithmic or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same VOC/COCO haze and low-light variants, RTTS, ExDark, and motion-blur, rain, snow, and haze–rain scenarios. The checklist's contradictory user-study statements provide no documented additional evaluation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including the restoration cascades, IA, GDIP, FeatEnHancer, and SNR/PGD ablations. Appendix revisions change score assignments without adding or removing comparison methods.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 and Appendix C retain the same splits, degradation generation, metrics, detector configurations, preprocessing, and training budgets. The revised appendix tables report the same experimental conditions.

E4.justification: The component, alternative-regularizer, sharing-depth, and coefficient ablations remain unchanged, as do generalization tests, restoration-only analysis, and qualitative stability comparisons in the main text and appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Checklist item 7 newly acknowledges the existing absence of error bars but introduces no uncertainty estimates or statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 12 and 14 exchange YOLOv10/YOLOv8 numerical blocks for all-object haze and dark evaluations and ExDark. For LR-YOLOv10, Table 12's VOC_Haze_Val/RTTS all-object mAP changes from 76.5/42.4 to 74.4/38.5; Table 14's VOC_Dark_Val all-object/ExDark mAP changes from 63.9/54.5 to 62.7/53.8. LR-YOLOv8 receives the reverse assignments. These correct appendix attribution, bringing these aggregates into agreement with unchanged Table 1; they do not establish new runs or performance gains.

T1.justification: The Lipschitz definitions, formal assumptions, Remarks 3–4, and Appendix A proof are unchanged. The checklist references the existing proof without adding mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about cascaded Lipschitz mismatch and improved stability and accuracy through restoration learning and parameter-space regularization.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, interpretations of experiments, single-degradation limitation, future directions, and Appendix G broader-impact discussion are retained. The checklist supplies no substantive additional scientific interpretation or limitation analysis.

D1.justification: V2 adds a first-page repository link labeled 'Code available'; existing implementation details remain unchanged. The new checklist inconsistently denies open access and claims appendix PyTorch-like code that is not present. The PDFs establish an added access pointer, not verified repository contents.

R1.justification: Section 2 and all 37 research references are unchanged. The checklist's policy links do not revise the paper's relationship to prior research or novelty positioning.

P1.justification: V2 appends a 16-item NeurIPS checklist, including template instructions and guidelines, and lightly rewrites the acknowledgments while adding a grant. The original scientific narrative and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: All nine figures and fourteen tables retain their designs, captions, and placement; numerical corrections use the existing table layouts. Limited layout changes comprise the added code footnote, acknowledgment/reference reflow, and formatted checklist pages.

improvement.justification: Correcting model attribution in Tables 12 and 14 resolves concrete inconsistencies between appendix LR-YOLO results and unchanged Table 1, improving interpretability. The code pointer also improves discoverability. These limited gains are tempered by new checklist defects: unsupported appendix-code claims and conflicting code-access and human-study statements. The core method, experimental scope, and principal evidence remain unchanged.
